newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crude rises amid thin regional talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crude rises amid thin regional talk.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices crudes rose Wednesday in line with gains in other regional markets, traders said.

West Coast trade remained quiet while oil companies planned how to move their crude into refineries in July. Last minute deals for July deliveries of Alaskan and California fell through, traders said, leaving discounts for local crude oils unchanged from Tuesday.
The price for Alaskan North Slope (ANS) crude, the regional benchmark, remained at $2.16 under July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) crude.
California Kern River crude rose on talk of a deal done 10 cents over posted prices, or at around $13.23 a barrel.
Also, Line 63 barrels were heard done 15 cents firmer at 90 cents over California Buena Vista crude prices, or at $15.76 a barrel.
-- David Brinkerhoff, New York Oil Desk +1 212 859 1633
